canonicalName: Kepler's laws: conic geometry into planetary astronomy

milestones.label: Elliptical orbit and area law in Astronomia nova
milestones.description: Kepler presents the elliptical orbit of Mars and the equal-areas rule.

evidence.claim: Published 1609; presents elliptical orbit and area law (Ch. 59)

notes: Wikipedia pages for Harmonices Mundi and the Kepler's-laws article timed out or were blocked; 1619 third law unverified here and not included. No naming/institution milestone sought.

canonicalName: Jacobi: theta functions and elliptic function theory

milestones.label: Fundamenta nova published
milestones.work: Jacobi, Fundamenta nova theoriae functionum ellipticarum, 1829
milestones.description: Jacobi's treatise introduces Jacobi elliptic functions and the triple product identity.
milestones.note: Page does not explicitly mention theta functions; 1827 catalogue start date unverified.

notes: Only Wikipedia checked; no first_statement separated (1827 announcements unverified).

canonicalName: Plucker: line geometry and algebraic curves

milestones.label: Theorie der algebraischen Kurven (Plucker equations)
milestones.description: Work on algebraic curves including the Plucker equations relating order and class.

evidence.claim: MacTutor dates the work to 1839 and the Plucker equations

milestones.label: Neue Geometrie des Raumes, line as space element
milestones.description: Line geometry: part 1 published 1868, part 2 completed by Klein 1869.

evidence.claim: MacTutor: first part 1868, second 1869 by Klein

notes: Catalogue range 1865-1868 for line geometry not confirmed (MacTutor gives 1868/1869). 1835 System der analytischen Geometrie noted but not milestoned.

milestones.label: Natural and Political Observations
milestones.work: Graunt, Natural and Political Observations Made upon the Bills of Mortality, 1662
milestones.description: Analysis of London bills of mortality yielding the first life table.

evidence.claim: Published 1662 (Old Style; 1663 New Style); credited with first life table

notes: Halley's refinement not verified (page does not mention it).

milestones.label: Memoir on double-curvature curves completed at age 16
milestones.work: Clairaut, research on curves of double curvature, 1729
milestones.description: Clairaut completes the research presented to the Paris Academy.

milestones.label: Recherches sur les courbes a double courbure published
milestones.work: Clairaut, Recherches sur les courbes a double courbure, 1731
milestones.description: Published study of space curves by analytic geometry and calculus.

notes: Single-source check (Wikipedia/MacTutor); no further sources opened.

canonicalName: Huygens: evolutes and the isochronous pendulum

milestones.label: Cycloid pendulum discovered
milestones.description: Huygens finds the pendulum is isochronous on a cycloid.

milestones.label: Horologium oscillatorium published
milestones.description: Treatise proving tautochronism of the cycloid and introducing evolutes and involutes.

evidence.claim: Published 1673; Part II tautochrone, Part III evolutes

notes: Single-source check (Wikipedia/MacTutor); no further sources opened.

canonicalName: Saint-Vincent and Sarasa: area under hyperbola and logarithm

milestones.label: Opus geometricum: equal hyperbola areas for equal ratios
milestones.work: Gregoire de Saint-Vincent, Opus geometricum, Antwerp, 1647
milestones.description: Shows hyperbola areas over intervals with equal endpoint ratios are equal, leading to the logarithm.

notes: Sarasa's logarithm link: no year on the page; not milestoned. Leibniz dy/y unverified.

canonicalName: Islamic work on the parallel postulate
notes: Only Wikipedia Saccheri quadrilateral page read (Khayyam late 11th c.; Ibn al-Haytham and Tusi not mentioned); no per-work dated source opened. Left empty.
Wikipedia Celestial element method opened; gives no dates for Ce yuan hai jing (1248) or Siyuan yujian (1303). Dates unverified; left empty.

milestones.label: Arithmetica infinitorum
milestones.description: Interpolation extends Cavalieri's indivisibles and yields the Wallis product for pi.

notes: Single-source check (Wikipedia/MacTutor); no further sources opened.

milestones.label: Chandahshastra (c. 3rd-2nd c. BCE)
milestones.description: Recursive enumeration of light/heavy syllable patterns and the meru-prastara array.

evidence.claim: Dated c. 3rd or 2nd century BCE; binary-like method and triangular array

milestones.note: Year is a midpoint of an uncertain range; Halayudha 10th c. commentary noted, not milestoned.

notes: Precision should be read as a range of centuries.

canonicalName: Babylonian astronomical parameters enter Greek astronomy

milestones.label: Hipparchus tests lunar models on Babylonian data
milestones.description: Hipparchus fitted lunar models to Babylonian eclipses and used Babylonian periods.

evidence.claim: Page: fitted model to Babylonian eclipses 383-382 BC; first to use Babylonian techniques systematically; active c.162-127 BC

milestones.note: Midpoint year; Hipparchus' works are lost, reconstruction via Ptolemy.

notes: Scholarly dispute on direction of transmission noted by the page.
